name: Repair equipment and rebuild pumps
summary: When a frac pump, blender, cementing or coiled tubing unit or tractor fails or comes back from the field with a defect, a planner opens a repair order and the shop manager ranks it against what the fleets need next. Heavy-duty technicians diagnose the fault, the shop manager approves the estimate, and fluid end and power end technicians, mechanics, electricians or welders repair the unit before it is tested and signed off. Parts back orders, a shortage of bays and technicians, and repeat failures from poor seating or misdiagnosis decide how long units are down and how many pumps a fleet can field.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight crewed frac fleets, about 16 cementing units and six coiled tubing crews, maintained from district shops in Alberta and northeast BC.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: an ERP plant maintenance module for work orders, hour readings from engine controllers and the data van, paper or tablet checklists, spreadsheets and phone calls between shops and field crews.

trigger: A crew defect write-up, a field mechanic's repair request, a PM finding or a pump failure during a job asks the shop to repair a unit.
end_state: The unit is repaired, tested, signed off and shown as available to operations, with the work order closed; or the unit is tagged out and parked for capital review.

volume.seasonality: Follows active equipment: highest in the winter drilling season and in spring break-up when parked units are torn down and rebuilt, lower in summer and much lower in 2020 when crews were parked.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume. About 60 per cent of repair orders come from defects written up by crews and found when units return to the yard, the rest from field breakdowns, PM findings and pump failures logged as non-productive time. Fluid end spending of $7.5-8.0 million a year (src1) at roughly $100,000-150,000 per stainless fluid end implies 50-80 fluid end replacements a year, a small share of repair orders; valves, seats, packing, engines and welding make up the rest.

surge.cause: Spring break-up: road bans park the fleet and equipment comes into the shops for overhaul

evidence.note: Spring break-up weight limits reduce oilfield activity (src1); spring thaw road bans start when thaw depth reaches 25 cm (src6). Duration and shop multiplier are tier C, matching the organisation file.
Diagnosis, engine and transmission repairs, reassembly, testing and close-out on about 500 repair orders a month.

roles.title: Fluid end and power end technician

evidence.note: Fluid end, valve, seat and packing repairs and power end rebuilds (rebuilds worked in pairs).
Frame, trailer, bracket and manifold welding repairs.
Controls, wiring harness and sensor repairs.
Prioritises the repair queue against fleet needs, approves estimates and signs off work.
Opens repair orders, expedites parts, reviews costs and files warranty claims. Not listed on this process in the organisation file.
Picks and issues repair parts. Not listed on this process in the organisation file.
Approves major repair spend above the shop manager's limit. Not listed on this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Maintenance work order and equipment history module
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
Vehicle telematics and electronic driver logs
Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones

resources.name: Heavy equipment service bay (drive-through bay with overhead crane) in a district maintenance shop
Frac pump unit (2,500 to 3,000 HHP, trailer mounted)

steps.name: Open the repair work order
steps.description: The maintenance planner reads the defect write-up, field mechanic's note or non-productive time report, checks the unit's history in the maintenance module for repeat failures and warranty status, and opens a corrective work order with the reported symptoms and priority asked for by operations.

error.defect_description: Vague symptoms or the wrong unit number on the work order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Prioritise against fleet needs
steps.description: At the morning shop meeting the shop manager ranks open repairs by which units the frac, cementing and coiled tubing fleets need for their next jobs, how many spare pumps each fleet has, and which technicians and bays are free.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Bring the unit in and lock it out
steps.description: When a bay and technician come free, the heavy-duty technician moves the unit into the bay, shuts it down, applies personal locks to the battery disconnect and engine start, bleeds the fluid end and verifies the engine will not start.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15, sections 212-214: isolate machinery and equipment, verify isolation and apply personal locks before maintenance

evidence.note: Isolation and personal locks (src5). Waits for bays and technicians tier C.

steps.name: Diagnose the fault
steps.description: The technician reproduces the fault where possible, reads engine and transmission codes with the OEM laptop software, inspects for leaks, cracks and wear, and on pumps pulls valve covers or checks crosshead clearances. The finding and likely parts go on the work order.

error.defect_description: Misdiagnosis: the wrong component is replaced and the fault returns on test.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Write the repair estimate
steps.description: The technician lists the parts with part numbers from the parts catalogue and estimates labour hours, so the shop manager can compare the repair cost with the unit's value and the fleet's need for it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Approve the repair scope
steps.description: The shop manager checks the estimate against the unit's age, repeat failures and whether a newer unit could take its place, approves repairs within the shop limit, sends large ones to the director, and marks obsolete units that are not worth repairing.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority: repair spend above the shop manager's limit needs director approval

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Approve major repair spend
steps.description: The director of equipment maintenance reviews large repairs such as engine or power end replacements, compares them with the capital plan for upgrades, and approves, defers or sends the unit for capital review.

control.basis: Company delegation of authority for maintenance spend

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Pick and issue the repair parts
steps.description: A warehouse attendant picks the listed parts from the base stores, issues them to the work order in the ERP and brings them to the bay. Parts that are not on the shelf or are counted wrong are reported to the planner.

error.defect_description: A part is issued to the wrong order or taken without a transaction.

next.condition: fluid end, valves, seats or packing

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Expedite the missing parts
steps.description: The planner checks stock at other bases, phones suppliers and dealers for availability, raises an urgent requisition for the buyer, and tells operations when the unit is likely to be back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Wait for the supplier to deliver
steps.description: The part comes from another base, a dealer in Edmonton or Calgary, or a manufacturer in the United States. Engines, transmissions and fluid ends had long lead times in 2021-2022, and the unit sits torn down in a bay or in the yard meanwhile.

next.condition: fluid end, valves, seats or packing

evidence.note: Long lead times on key parts (src1). Waits are tier C.

steps.name: Repair the fluid end, valves, seats or packing
steps.description: A fluid end and power end technician replaces worn valves, seats, springs and packing, or lifts off a cracked or washed fluid end with the bay crane and fits a rebuilt or new one, with a second technician helping on the lift, then torques the stay rods to specification.

error.defect_description: A seat is not fully seated or torque is wrong, causing a washout on the first job.

evidence.note: Fluid ends wear from abrasive slurry at up to 15,000 psi and are replaced as modular units; $7.5 million spent on fluid ends in 2022 (src1). Minutes tier C.

steps.name: Rebuild the power end
steps.description: Two technicians remove the power end, strip it, measure the crankshaft, bearings, connecting rods and crossheads, replace worn parts, reassemble with new seals and run it in on the test stand.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Repair the engine, transmission or driveline
steps.description: The heavy-duty technician replaces failed engine components, turbochargers, injectors, cooling parts or transmission modules, or removes the engine or transmission when it needs an overhaul the shop does not do.

error.defect_description: A connection or sensor is left loose after the repair.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Wait for the dealer overhaul
steps.description: The engine or transmission goes to the OEM dealer for overhaul or exchange and comes back for the technician to reinstall. Dealer queues and core exchange stock decide how long the unit is down.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Repair electrical and controls
steps.description: The electrical and instrumentation technician traces wiring faults, replaces harnesses, sensors and controller modules, and reloads controller settings from the OEM software.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Weld and fabricate the repair
steps.description: The welder cuts out and replaces cracked brackets, trailer cross members, decks or guards, or repairs low-pressure manifold piping, following the shop's welding procedure, and paints the repair.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Reassemble, unlock and test the unit
steps.description: The heavy-duty technician reassembles guards and covers, checks that everyone is clear, removes the locks, runs the unit to temperature and on pumps pumps water against a test choke to look for leaks, knocks and fault codes.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code Part 15, section 215.3: returning equipment to operation after locks are removed

evidence.note: Returning equipment to operation after lockout (src5). Failure share tier C.

steps.name: Sign off the repair
steps.description: The shop manager or lead hand walks round the unit, checks the torque and test sheet and signs the work order before the unit leaves the shop.

control.basis: Company quality procedure: supervisor sign-off before a repaired pressure pumping unit returns to service

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Close the work order with failure codes
steps.description: The technician types labour hours, parts used, the failure code and cause from the paper job card into the maintenance module and sets the order to technically complete.

error.defect_description: Missing or generic failure code, or labour hours left off.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Review costs and failure data
steps.description: The planner checks parts issued against the job card, corrects failure codes, compares the cost with the estimate and flags units under OEM warranty.

control.basis: Maintenance records per unit kept for warranty claims, insurers and customer equipment audits

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: File a warranty claim with the manufacturer
steps.description: The planner gathers the work order, failure photos, hour readings and parts invoices and submits a warranty claim through the dealer or OEM portal, then tracks the credit in a spreadsheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Update fleet availability
steps.description: The planner marks the unit available on the dispatch board and the weekly fleet status sheet and tells the district or frac operations coordinator that it is ready.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

steps.name: Tag the unit out and request a capital review
steps.description: The shop manager tags the unit out of service, writes a short note with the repair estimate and condition for the director and finance, and the unit goes to the parked line until an upgrade, rebuild or sale is decided.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of heavy equipment maintenance in WCSB pressure pumping companies.

exceptions.name: Parts not in stock
exceptions.description: A part is short or on back order; the planner expedites and the unit waits days to weeks.

exceptions.name: Component sent to the dealer
exceptions.description: An engine or transmission needs an overhaul the shop does not do and goes to the OEM dealer.

exceptions.name: Failed test after repair
exceptions.description: The fault returns or a new leak appears on test and the unit goes back to diagnosis.

exceptions.name: Not worth repairing
exceptions.description: The estimate exceeds the unit's value or fits a planned upgrade, so the unit is parked for capital review.

exceptions.name: Warranty claim
exceptions.description: The failure is under OEM warranty and the planner files a claim.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from repair order opened to closed
benchmarks.population: Corrective repair orders on pressure pumping units at a WCSB service company, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: most repairs finish within a week once a bay is free; parts back orders and dealer overhauls make a long tail of three to eight weeks. No published figure found.

benchmarks.population: Trican Well Service, stainless steel fluid ends in repair and maintenance expense

pain_points.description: Parts back orders leave torn-down units in bays for weeks, worst in 2021-2022, and reduce how many pumps a fleet can field.

evidence.note: Long lead times on key parts (src1); duration tier C.

pain_points.description: Too few bays and technicians for the repair queue, so units wait in the yard and the shop manager re-ranks the queue every morning as fleet needs change.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of shop capacity against the organisation file volumes; the public results opened describe hiring difficulty for field crews, not shops.

pain_points.description: Fluid end costs are large and variable, and early failures from poor seating or misdiagnosis repeat the repair.

evidence.note: Fluid ends drive variability in repair and maintenance expense (src1).

pain_points.description: Failure codes and labour are typed in late from paper job cards, so repeat-failure analysis and warranty recovery are weak.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice.

sources.title: Trican Well Service Ltd. Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2022
sources.supports: Stainless steel fluid end costs of $7.5 million in 2022 and $8.0 million in 2021 ($1.2 million in Q4 2022) as the item that drives variability in repair and maintenance expense; higher active equipment raised repair and maintenance costs; personnel costs include operational support personnel such as mechanics; long lead times on key parts and record inflation in 2022; maintenance capital $29.96 million in 2022 and $23.5 million in 2021; fluid ends pump abrasive slurry at up to 15,000 psi and are modular units replaced independently of the power end; spring break-up road weight limits reduce oilfield activity; seven active and five parked frac crews in 2022.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code, Part 15: Managing the Control of Hazardous Energy
sources.supports: Part 15 sections 212 (isolation of machinery, equipment or powered mobile equipment), 213 (verifying isolation), 214 (assigning personal locks), 215 (group control procedures), 215.3 (returning to operation) and 215.4 (isolation of piping). Current page; Part 15 was in force in an earlier edition in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans reduce maximum weights on roads during weak or thawing conditions; spring heavy haul weights start when thaw depth reaches 25 cm; provincial highway and municipal bans; exemptions by permit from the Central Permit Office.

assumptions: The organisation file lists three triggers (field breakdowns, PM findings and frac non-productive time). Their volumes (about 60, 80 and 25 repair orders a month) add to about 170, a third of the 500 a month in the file. The rest are defects written up by crews and found when units return to the yard, so this file adds fo-dist-yard-and-base-operations as the largest trigger (60 per cent).

Repair types are mixed: fluid end, valve, seat and packing work 34 per cent, structural and welding 23, engine and transmission 27, electrical 13 and power end rebuilds 3. A power end rebuild every 5,000 to 8,000 pump hours across about 190 pumps gives about 10 to 15 a month (tier C).
Simple valve and seat swaps done by frac crews on location between stages are not shop repair orders and are left out.

The organisation file's maintenance-shop resource (5 at about 500 hours a month) is too small for the bay time of repairs and services, so a service bay resource of about 40 bays is used, as in the preventive maintenance file.

The frac-pump resource is held only during hands-on repair steps, because its cost per hour is a running cost; units also sit out of service during parts and dealer waits (a median of about five days when a part is short), which a capacity model should count as lost availability rather than running cost. For non-pump units the hours apply to the unit being repaired.
A unit parked for capital review leaves this process; the organisation file has no link from this process to capital planning or asset disposal, so one is added.

Staffing: about 42 FTE of technicians and welders plus planners, warehouse and supervision, close to the hands-on time times 500 orders a month at 130 productive hours. With preventive maintenance (about 41 technician FTE) this uses about 80 of the 127 shop technicians in the organisation file; the rest go to iron, inspections, manufacturing and leave.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.35).
